name: Miqie
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Gao 2017 UH dissertation (read online, ScholarSpace hdl 10125/62498) is contact/vitality-focused with no stress statement; no phonology of Miqie located.

sources.citation: archive.org item lifegeoffreycha00godwgoog, catalogued as Zhu Wenxu 2005 彝语方言学 Yiyu fangyanxue
sources.note: Irrelevant: the scan is actually Godwin's Life of Geoffrey Chaucer (mis-catalogued); discarded.

sources.citation: Gao, Katie B. 2017. Dynamics of Language Contact in China: Ethnolinguistic Diversity and Variation in Yunnan. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa (ScholarSpace hdl 10125/62498).
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 4.3.2.1 (p.70-71) gives a short phonological profile: (C)V syllables, 'every syllable contains a lexical tone', consonant/rhyme/tone tables (tones 55, 33, 21/31, and a Miqie-only rising 25); p.~93 notes phrase-final intonation realizes the rising tone as mid level (tone sandhi). The words stress/accent occur only in non-linguistic senses.

sources.citation: Gao, Katie B. 2015. Assessing the Linguistic Vitality of Miqie: An Endangered Ngwi (Loloish) Language of Yunnan, China. Language Documentation & Conservation 9: 164-191 (hdl 10125/24640).
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic vitality survey. p.167 identifies the only other description of the language: Yang Limei 2007, a ten-page sketch (wordlist, phonology, syntax) published internally by the Chuxiong Institute for Yi Studies, hard copy only.
